english.title: Possess / control wireless telegraphy station / apparatus with intent self / another to use without section 8 licence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) possessed or had under your control

(A)_[a wireless telegraphy station,]_
(B)_[wireless telegraphy apparatus,]_

(C)_[intending to]_
(D)_[knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), intended to]_

use it for the purpose of making a broadcast, otherwise than in accordance with a wireless telegraphy licence granted by OFCOM under section 8 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006
english.legislation: Contrary to section 36(1) and (2) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 105 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(ii) Section 106 of the Act applies where a person is convicted of this offence and the use continues after the conviction.
(iii) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement regarding this offence.
(iv) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16(a) of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
